language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.
Hi, I am Sara. Nice to meet you! Have you ever tossed a ball in the air? Have you ever dropped a ball? What happens? It hits the ground, right?

There are forces that help the ball move like that: pushing, pulling and....gravity! Gravity is the natural force that makes things fall towards the ground, the heavier the object the bigger the force of gravity. You cannot see these forces, but we use them every day to play, move and travel around.
Will you help me see how these forces work as I help my Dad move toys from his store to my Uncle's?
You will use these forces; pushes, pulls and gravity to explore how things move. Let's go!

The toys have arrived safely at my uncle’s store in Italy. Have you ever been to Italy? They sure love football here! Some kids invited me to play with them. Perhaps what I’ve learned about forces will come in handy.

Let's see:
Kicks and jumps = pushes,
catches = pulls,
gravity = the force pulling objects to the ground.
Right? Let's see how this works in a football game!
